what: highlight "prevented 1.33 million sales between 2022Q2 and 2023Q4"
said: In March twenty twenty-four, the Federal Housing Finance Agency published a strange number. One point three three million American home sales that should have happened, and never did.

source: FRED, Median Sales Price of New Houses
what: highlight "Q2 2026: 410,700"
said: Except they didn't. The typical new house in America still sells for over four hundred ten thousand dollars.
And the thirty-year mortgage rate this week is still above seven percent.

what: highlight "2025: 87,460"
said: In twenty twenty-five, the median American household earned about eighty-seven thousand dollars a year.

source: FRED, Median Sales Price of New Houses
what: highlight "410,700"
said: The median new house sold for about four hundred ten thousand. That's almost five years of your entire pay, before taxes, food, or anything else.

what: highlight "nearly all 50 million active mortgages have fixed rates"
said: The FHFA paper says nearly all fifty million active mortgages in the United States have fixed rates.

what: highlight "most have interest rates far below prevailing market rates, creating a disincentive to sell"
said: The paper puts it plainly. Most of these loans sit far below today's rates, which creates a disincentive to sell.

what: highlight "the probability of sale is decreased by 18.1%"
said: And they measured it. For every one point that today's rate sits above yours, your chance of selling falls by eighteen point one percent.

what: highlight "led to a 57% reduction in home sales with fixed-rate mortgages in 2023Q4"
said: By the end of twenty twenty-three, that lock-in alone had cut sales of homes with fixed-rate loans by fifty-seven percent.

what: highlight "results in people not living in homes they would prefer"
said: People call these golden handcuffs. The rate is so good it keeps you in a house you might not even want anymore. Like keeping a gym membership you never use, because the old price will never come back.

what: highlight "which decreased prices by 3.3%"
said: The FHFA did the math on both sides. Higher rates on their own pushed prices down by three point three percent.

what: highlight "The supply reduction increased home prices by 5.7%"
said: But the missing sellers pushed prices up by five point seven percent. The tool built to cool prices froze the sellers instead. And prices went up.

what: highlight "the U.S. housing shortage has declined slightly to 3.7 million units"
said: Freddie Mac, the government-backed mortgage company, estimates the country is short three point seven million homes.

what: highlight "Despite adding 5.8 million housing units over approximately four years"
said: America did build again. Five point eight million homes in about four years. But demand grew almost as fast, so the hole barely shrank.

what: highlight "75% of land zoned for residential uses is zoned single-family"
said: In many American cities, about seventy-five percent of the land for homes allows only one thing. A single detached house on its own lot.

what: highlight "94% San Jose, California"
said: In San Jose, California, it's ninety-four percent.

what: highlight "originated in 1916 in the Elmwood neighborhood of Berkeley, California"
said: The rule goes back to nineteen sixteen, in the Elmwood neighborhood of Berkeley, California.

what: highlight "Single-family zoning both increases the cost of housing units and decreases the supply."
said: And the effect is simple. When you can only build one home where four could fit, you get fewer homes, and each one costs more.

what: highlight "opposition by residents to proposed real estate and infrastructure developments in their local area"
said: And when a builder asks to build more, local residents often show up to stop it. There's even a name for that. NIMBY. Not in my back yard.

what: highlight "bought 1,000 distressed houses in Phoenix, Arizona"
said: After the two thousand eight crash, millions of homes were foreclosed. Between twenty ten and twenty eleven, a company called Treehouse bought one thousand distressed houses in Phoenix, Arizona.

what: highlight "The company was acquired by Blackstone Inc in the spring of 2012"
said: In twenty twelve, Blackstone bought it and formed Invitation Homes.

what: highlight "the company owned 86,192 rental homes"
said: By December twenty twenty-five, it owned eighty-six thousand one hundred ninety-two rental homes.

what: highlight "30% were all-cash buyers"
said: The National Association of Realtors found that thirty percent of repeat buyers paid all cash.

what: highlight "Gifts or loans from family and friends (22%)"
said: And first-time buyers who did make it? Twenty-two percent used gifts or loans from family and friends for the down payment. The bank of mom and dad.

what: highlight "dropped to a record low of 21%"
said: The same report gave two records on the same day. First-time buyers made up just twenty-one percent of all home purchases. The lowest share ever recorded.

what: highlight "climbed to an all-time high of 40 years"
said: And the typical first-time buyer was forty years old. The oldest ever recorded.

what: highlight "contracted by 50% since 2007"
said: That share has shrunk by half since two thousand seven.

what: highlight "Delayed or denied homeownership until age 40 instead of 30 can mean losing roughly $150,000 in equity on a typical starter home."
said: And waiting costs you real money. NAR's estimate: buying at forty instead of thirty can mean losing about one hundred fifty thousand dollars of equity on a starter home.

what: highlight "Median time in home before selling: 11 years"
said: Meanwhile, owners stay put longer than ever. The typical seller had lived in their home for eleven years. Another all-time high.

what: highlight "Certain borrower groups with lower wealth accumulation are less able to strategically time their sales, worsening inequality"
said: And the FHFA paper adds one more line. People with less wealth are the least able to time their sales, which makes inequality worse.

what: highlight "In 2018, Minneapolis became the first major city in the US to end single-family zoning"
said: Some places changed the rules. In twenty eighteen, Minneapolis became the first major American city to end single-family zoning.

what: highlight "SB 1069 and AB 2299 are California bills approved in 2016"
said: California went after backyards. In twenty sixteen it passed laws that limit how much cities can block small backyard homes.

what: highlight "allow the purchaser of a home to take over the existing terms of the mortgage including; the interest rate"
said: And some loans are assumable. A buyer can take over the seller's loan, including the old low rate.

what: highlight "Mortgage assumptions have gained popularity since 2022"
said: Those deals have grown since twenty twenty-two, for exactly this reason. But most loans don't allow it.
